context.title: Enable the DCGM exporter on Civo, document it for existing clusters
context.body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to Modelplane! Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR
and follow it, especially the commit, pull request, and writing style
conventions: https://github.com/modelplaneai/modelplane/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
PRs that don't follow it will be closed.
-->

### Description of your changes

On a Civo cluster Modelplane provisions, every `modelplane_gpu_*` series and `modelplane_energy_joules_total` was empty. The hand-written Civo stack disabled the GPU Operator's DCGM exporter - not catched as other handwritten installing the GPU Operator as pre-req.
The telemetry collector discovers a GPU exporter by pod label, so with no exporter DaemonSet there was nothing to scrape.

This enables the exporter on Civo with the same `dcgm`/`dcgmExporter` values the generated clouds pin, so one review moves both halves; the metrics CSV covers every field `metrics.py` maps. The gpu-operator chart gains a kube-prometheus-stack edge: unlike the generated clouds, Civo's kube-prometheus-stack keeps its bundled CRDs enabled, so that release is what provides the ServiceMonitor CRD, and it now sets `wait=True` as a depended-on chart must.

On `source: Existing` clusters Modelplane doesn't install an exporter, on purpose: it can't know whether the cluster already runs one, and the collector scrapes every pod matching `.*dcgm.*`, so a second exporter would collect each GPU twice. The docs now say so. A new GPUs section in the telemetry page documents the discovery contract, the seven DCGM fields with their unit conversions, and how to check what an exporter publishes; the existing-cluster requirements gain a DCGM exporter bullet pointing at it.

### Validated

on a live Civo NYC1 cluster: all seven renamed series arrive at the collector's debug sink.

```
    kubectl logs deploy/modelplane-collector -n modelplane-system | grep -E 'modelplane_gpu_|modelplane_energy' | sort -u
    -> Name: modelplane_energy_joules_total
    -> Name: modelplane_gpu_compute_active_ratio
    -> Name: modelplane_gpu_memory_bandwidth_ratio
    -> Name: modelplane_gpu_memory_used_bytes
    -> Name: modelplane_gpu_power_watts

```

closingIssuesReferences.body:
### What happened?

GPU metrics aren't generated on `source: Existing` clusters. On existing clusters Modelplane doesn't install a GPU exporter, and [Requirements for an existing cluster](https://github.com/modelplaneai/modelplane/blob/v0.5.0/docs/content/platform/inference-cluster.md#requirements-for-an-existing-cluster) doesn't say one is needed. [Telemetry](https://github.com/modelplaneai/modelplane/blob/v0.5.0/docs/content/platform/telemetry.md) only says the collector reads "the GPU exporter your cloud provides".

We expect the requirements for an existing cluster to include the instructions to get GPU metrics.

### How can we reproduce it?

This comes from a user's report on v0.5.0 and from reading the docs and code. We haven't reproduced it on a cluster ourselves.

1. Import a GPU cluster with `source: Existing` that doesn't run a DCGM exporter.
2. Deploy a model on it and send it some requests.
3. Engine and gateway metrics arrive at the sink. No `modelplane_gpu_*` series do.

### What environment did it happen in?

Modelplane version: v0.5.0

- Cluster imported with `source: Existing`. We don't have the user's cloud, Kubernetes version or GPU type.
- The docs and code are the same on main (1b3046ef).
closingIssuesReferences.title: Docs don't say how to get GPU metrics on a `source: Existing` cluster
